Pluck field returns incorrect data structure when nested object is None

#### Description

When using a `Pluck` field with a nested object that is `None`, the field returns an empty dictionary `{}` instead of `None`. This breaks existing code that expects `None` values to be preserved.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from marshmallow import Schema, fields

class UserSchema(Schema):
    name = fields.Str()
    age = fields.Int()

class BlogSchema(Schema):
    title = fields.Str()
    user = fields.Pluck(UserSchema, 'name')

# Create a blog with no user
blog_data = {'title': 'My Blog', 'user': None}
schema = BlogSchema()
result = schema.dump(blog_data)

print(f"Expected: {{'title': 'My Blog', 'user': None}}")
print(f"Actual: {result}")
```

The output shows that `user` is `{}` instead of `None`, which is unexpected behavior. This also affects the `many=True` case where individual None values in collections are converted to empty dictionaries.
</issue>
